headline: AI Trade Buckles as Homebuilders and Defensives Take the Lead
body_html:
Thursday's session belonged to the sellers of artificial intelligence. Semiconductors sank 6.63%, by far the weakest group we track, as commentary around the close pointed to a perfect storm hitting the Nasdaq and a flight toward defensive shares. The damage was concentrated, though: of 544 stocks in our universe, 303 rose and 237 fell.

The rotation was unmistakable. Homebuilders jumped 5.98%, consumer names added 2.76%, software gained 2.07% and healthcare rose 1.38%. On the other side, energy lost 2.09% even with Gulf security headlines flashing, while materials slipped 1.16% and industrials 1.10%. Money appeared to leave the crowded AI complex and settle in housing, household spending and other more defensive corners.

The standout mover was Forgent Power Solutions, down 21.54%, the steepest drop in our universe. Carpenter Technology fell 20.62% and Vicor 15.66%. Vital Farms led the gainers at 15.18%. The close leaves a market whose leadership flipped in a single day, and Friday will test whether that shift holds or proves a one-session reflex.

briefs.headline: Chip Complex Takes the Brunt
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 6.63%, the worst showing of any group we follow. Chip-equipment maker FormFactor dropped 15.29% and power-module supplier Vicor lost 15.66%. Selling reached well beyond the largest names and into the suppliers that serve the AI buildout.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Lead the Tape
briefs.body: Homebuilders climbed 5.98%, the best sector result of the session. The move came as investors rotated away from technology and toward businesses tied to housing. It stood out in a day when most of the market's attention was on the AI selloff.

briefs.headline: Household Names Catch a Bid
briefs.body: Consumer shares rose 2.76%. Winnebago Industries gained 11.43% and Mohawk Industries 9.03%. Vital Farms jumped 15.18% and WD-40 Company added 9.15%. Buyers favored companies tied to homes, leisure and everyday goods.

briefs.headline: Industrials Split Down the Middle
briefs.body: The industrials group slipped 1.10%, but the average hid a wide gap. Badger Meter surged 13.48% and Allegion rose 11.02%. MSC Industrial Direct and Graco each lost more than 15%. Stock-specific news mattered more than the sector label.

briefs.headline: Energy Slides Despite Gulf Tension
briefs.body: Energy fell 2.09% even as reports described fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and an evacuation order at Aramco's Dhahran headquarters. Citi argued that oil risks still lean to the upside. Traders did not carry that view into energy equities today.

briefs.headline: Labor Market Stays Remarkably Tight
briefs.body: Weekly jobless claims remain near their lowest level since the 1960s, extending a low-layoff trend. A resilient labor market lends support to consumer-facing shares. It also leaves investors weighing strong underlying data against Thursday's unsettled tone in technology.
